routes.reason: Source additions to GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands across GS.0–GS.7, 35 items, and the reason establishes something important: this paper IS that roadmap's own named source, GS.0's source route reading 'V. Lafforgue global bundle/level setup', GS.1's 'V. Lafforgue geometric Satake input', GS.2's 'V. Lafforgue shtuka construction', GS.3's 'V. Lafforgue Hecke-finite cohomology' and so on. That is why 41 of this extraction's 51 items are planned rather than missing — an unusual distribution that is exactly right here, and which a reviewer should check rather than flag.

A second source route to the same roadmap, 5 items, for the things in the paper that are in the direction of GS.3–GS.5 but that no stage plans — the Eichler–Shimura relations of Proposition 7.1 foremost among them. Separating these from route 1 is the right structure: route 1 records what the roadmap already names this paper for, route 2 records what it does not yet cover.

Source additions to LanglandsParameterStacks at LP2 and LP3, 4 items, and the best-argued route of the four. It sets out precisely what LP2 and LP3 already own — the excursion algebra, the coarse quotient, Fargues–Scholze VIII.3.8, the integral invariant theory — and then isolates what none of them states and what the argument turns on: the CHARACTERISTIC-ZERO invariant theory, that a tuple in H(Q̄_ℓ)^n is semisimple exactly when its diagonal conjugation orbit is closed (Richardson), so that the Q̄_ℓ-points of H^n//H are the semisimple conjugacy classes. It names Proposition 11.7 and Lemme 11.10 as what reconstructs σ for a profinite group and a possibly disconnected H, observes that the string 'pseudo-character' occurs nowhere in the atlas, and concludes 'Plan it once here, in characteristic zero for a profinite group and a possibly disconnected reductive H, and let both LP2:semisimple-characters and GS.5 import it.' I reviewed PAPER-BOCKLE-HARRIS-KHARE-ETAL-19 immediately before this job, and its route to the same stage records that IT proves the integral form, 'in a stronger form than the characteristic-zero statements that PAPER-LAFFORGUE-18 routes' there. The two extractions are mutually consistent and cross-referencing, which is precisely what two papers feeding one stage at different generality should look like.

One source item to MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.4. MP.4 owns the adelic metaplectic cover and the global Weil representation for the classical metaplectic group, and §14 of this paper indicates how the method adapts to metaplectic covers of a reductive group over a function field. A single addition to the right owner, and the reason is careful to present §14 as an indication rather than a theorem.

notes: Independent review by Claude Code, session cc-d67081, 23 September 2026, of the extraction by cc-442dc5. Verdict accept: no item, status, route or locator changed. All 51 items, 4 routes and 12 recorded mistakes were checked against arXiv 1209.5352v10, re-fetched and hashing to b37715f9…4295, matching the record; 184 pages in French. THE CLAIM THAT THE PUBLISHED VERSION IS UNREACHABLE WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN TAKEN ON TRUST, because the same claim proved false in the paper this reviewer handled immediately before (PAPER-BOCKLE-HARRIS-KHARE-ETAL-19, where Acta Mathematica turned out to be open access). Here it holds. Unpaywall reports doi:10.1090/jams/897 as bronze open access with a publisher PDF at ams.org, but that URL returns HTTP 403 to curl and, to a browser user-agent, a 3 MB HTML bot interstitial rather than a PDF, and the r.jina.ai proxy returns the JAMS issue listing instead of the article. The extraction's statement is therefore correct, and a publishedVersionCheck record noting this has been added to the source block so the next worker need not repeat the attempt. All 12 recorded mistakes are confirmed. Four were settled decisively. E3: p. 86 prints 'pr_1^*(F^{(I)}) et pr_1^*(F^{(I)})' — the same projection twice — while the sentence above introduces 'les projections pr_1 et pr_2'. E6: p. 154 says 'dans (12.1) la somme est indexée par ker^1(F,G)', but (12.1) on p. 150 is an inclusion with no sum in it; the decomposition indexed by ker^1(F,G) is (12.2), which p. 150 itself refers to twice. E8: Remarque 12.4 writes Q̄_ℓ on the left and E on the right of one displayed equality, where the ambient coefficient field is Q̄_ℓ. E12: 'éventuellemement' and 'mais mais' each occur exactly once in the 184 pages. For the remaining eight the quotation was verified and the verdict states what rests on the extraction. Three of them (E2, E9, E10) turn on a superscript or a tilde that the text layer flattens; the extraction records that it rendered page images for E9 and E10, which is the right standard, and this review corroborated E11's correction incidentally by reading the analogous display on p. 116 as an image, where the notation is H^{0,≤µ,E}_{N,I,W} with coefficient E and representation W. The extraction records no library items — right for this material — 41 planned items all naming atlas layers that exist, and 10 missing items routed exactly once. There is no run-together numbering. The unusual 41-planned-to-10-missing split is correct and route 1 explains it: this paper is the named source of GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands, stage by stage. All 4 routes are source additions; there is no Part II and no new roadmap, which for the paper a roadmap was already built from is plainly right. Route 3 deserves particular note, and this reviewer was able to check it across two jobs: it isolates the characteristic-zero invariant theory for LanglandsParameterStacks and says 'let both LP2:semisimple-characters and GS.5 import it', while PAPER-BOCKLE-HARRIS-KHARE-ETAL-19, reviewed immediately before, routes the INTEGRAL form to the same stage and says so explicitly. The two are mutually consistent and cross-referencing. Every check is listed in research/blueprint/reviews/REV-PAPER-LAFFORGUE-18.md.
